title: Context: Urgency MEDIUM 3/5, Importance CRITICAL 4/5, Depth DEEP 4/5 — Security & Keyring Package Migration (OPEN-001). We are replacing deprecated `keytar` with `@napi-rs/keyring` (Rust N-API package) for OS credential storage. On headless Linux servers, WSL, or Docker containers where no D-Bus session or Secret Service daemon (gnome-keyring / dbus-user-session) is running, `@napi-rs/keyring` throws runtime error `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown` on `setPassword()` / `getPassword()`. Answer with concrete numbers, tradeoff tables, code examples, and best-practice summaries: (1) Does `@napi-rs/keyring` still require libsecret / D-Bus Secret Service at runtime on Linux, or does its Rust backend bundle it? What are the exact runtime dependencies (libdbus, gnome-keyring, dbus-user-session, secret-service) and what errors appear when missing (ServiceUnknown, No such file, etc.) on headless/WSL/Docker? (2) How does `@napi-rs/keyring` compare to `keytar` regarding prebuilds, headless support, and D-Bus handling — tradeoff table (build deps, runtime deps, error modes, WSL behavior). (3) Recommended fallback: Should `UltronCoreBrain` catch keyring initialization errors and automatically failover to a file-permission-restricted local salt key (`~/.entity-agent/.vault_key` with `chmod 0600`) using Node `crypto` (e.g., AES-256-GCM with random 256-bit key)? Compare security tradeoffs vs OS keyring vs machine-id derived key vs plaintext, and provide production-ready try/catch fallback code with `securityLevel()` detection and user warning. Phrase to work verbatim on any AI chat platform.
